attendance: in-person attendance of 11,332 (overall attendance with hybrid more than 12,000)
attendance_method: ASA 2023 Annual Report loaded via curl with a browser UA (the fetch tool 403s on asahq.org). In the 'Our annual meeting was an outstanding success' paragraph: 'ANESTHESIOLOGY 2023 in San Francisco had an in-person attendance of 11,332; a 10% increase in attendance compared with 2022 and an overall attendance with hybrid of more than 12,000. 242 companies exhibited at the annual meeting.' The 11,332 in-person figure is used as the headline; it is not stated whether it excludes exhibitor staff, but it is explicitly in-person. The 2026 sponsorship prospectus (loaded, text extracted) contains no attendance number at all, only 'thousands of physician anesthesiologists', and the 2026 quick-facts PDF is logistics only. A search snippet asserting 'upwards of 15,000 attendees' at ANESTHESIOLOGY 2024 traced to a university department blog page which, when loaded, contains no such number — discarded.
ratio_rationale: Judged 18%, between ESC 15% and ASTRO 21%, and I am genuinely torn across that span — flagging the uncertainty rather than picking a confident number. The case for the low end: ANESTHESIOLOGY's bulk is refresher courses, problem-based learning discussions, workshops and panels taken for CME credit, which is the ESC shape. The case for the high end: ASA runs an unusually large contributed poster programme for a clinical congress, including a Medically Challenging Cases stream that exists specifically so that residents and fellows can present, and the 2023 meeting was a third residents and medical students — a cohort that submits heavily to exactly that stream, not lightly. (My first pass discounted them as low submitters; that was wrong and is corrected here.) 18% is where I land on balance.
programme_evidence: Sponsorship prospectus describes 'five days of education, scientific discovery, networking, and innovation' with 'expert-led education' and 'a robust exhibit hall'; the ASA annual report highlights PeRLS and POCUS workshops held at the meeting.
character_evidence: https://www.asahq.org/annualreport23 — abstract-based research is presented at the meeting ('research presented at ANESTHESIOLOGY 2023'), but the programme described in the sponsorship prospectus is dominated by expert-led education and workshops.

attendance: a record-breaking crowd of nearly 8,000 attendees, with 92% joining live on the convention floor
attendance_method: ASGCT 'Sponsor & Exhibit' page loaded via curl. The attendee-demographics block reads: 'We welcomed a record-breaking crowd of nearly 8,000 attendees, with an incredible 92% joining us live on the convention floor', alongside '20% of attendees traveled from outside the United States' and '64% of attendees work directly in an industry or corporate setting'. Explicitly virtual-inclusive: 92% on-site implies roughly 7,350 in the room. The figure describes the most recent completed meeting (the 28th, May 2025, New Orleans) as presented on the 2026 sponsor page. The /about page and the 2025 meeting page carry no number; the ASGCT attendee-summary document is behind member SSO.
ratio_rationale: Judged 25% of the full 8,000, against WCLC 25% and SABCS 21%. Applied to the whole headcount, not the on-site subset: the 8% who joined online are gene-therapy researchers presenting and viewing the same science, and an online abstract is still an abstract. Nor is the 64% industry-and-corporate share a reason to mark it down — in cell and gene therapy the biotech sector is where much of the primary science is generated, and those scientists submit to Molecular Therapy's meeting supplement like everyone else. What actually sets the level is the programme: a large open-call poster floor and oral abstract sessions carrying most of the content, which is the oncology-congress band. (My first pass stripped the virtual cohort and marked down the industry cohort; both were wrong and are corrected here, which moves this row up from 22%.)
programme_evidence: Sponsor page frames the audience as 'scientific leaders, biotech executives, investors, regulators, and clinicians'; the meeting's content is carried by a large contributed poster and oral-abstract programme.
character_evidence: https://annualmeeting.asgct.org/ — the meeting runs an open abstract call with a large poster programme; ASGCT publishes abstracts in Molecular Therapy.

attendance_method: The IADR 2025 IADR/PER General Session page (Barcelona, 25-28 June 2025) was loaded via curl and carries a post-meeting 'Meeting Stats' list: 'Total Attendance: 4,681 | Countries/Regions Represented: 96 | Oral Presentations: 354 | Distinguished Lectures Series Presentations: 3 | Poster Presentations: 2,595 | Symposia: 41 | Corporate Exhibit Booths: 17 | Institutional Exhibit Booths: 25'. 'Total Attendance' is not defined, so basis is UNSPECIFIED; with only 42 exhibit booths the exhibitor-staff inflation is small.
ratio_rationale: Not a judgement call here — the same source states the presentation counts. 354 oral + 2,595 poster presentations = 2,949 accepted presentations against 4,681 attendees, i.e. 63%. That sits between ATS 50% and GSA 119%, which is exactly where a dental-research general session belongs: almost everyone in the room is there to present their own work. Note this counts accepted presentations, so submissions were higher.
programme_evidence: 2,949 oral and poster presentations against 41 symposia and 23 hands-on workshops — the programme is overwhelmingly contributed science.
character_evidence: https://www.iadr.org/2025iags — open abstract call with a published deadline and notification cycle ('Abstract notification emails were sent to presenting authors'); abstracts archived at iadr.abstractarchives.com.

attendance: on average more than 5,000 surgeons, physicians, and other medical professionals

AAO-HNSF runs a real open abstract call feeding oral-paper and poster sessions, but the meeting's centre of gravity is instruction courses, miniseminars and hands-on surgical education bought for CME — the same balance as ASTRO, where a solid contributed track sits inside a large clinical teaching programme. Not pushed higher because a surgical academy meeting draws a large private-practice audience that attends to learn, not to present.
programme_evidence: Exhibit page sells access to attendees who 'understand the importance of coming for the world-class education'; the OTO EXPO with 225+ exhibitors is a major draw alongside the scientific programme.
character_evidence: https://www.entnet.org/events/annual-meeting/ — an open scientific-abstract call runs alongside an instruction-course-led programme.

attendance: the number of participants has averaged 1,300-1,500 participants
attendance_rung_name: prior editions, stated by a co-organising institute
attendance_method: LMU Klinikum Institute of Infectious Diseases and Tropical Medicine page for ECTMIH 2025 loaded via curl: 'With its most recent editions in Bergen, Norway in 2021, and Utrecht, Netherlands in 2023 the number of participants has averaged 1,300-1,500 participants.' No figure for the 2025 Hamburg edition itself was found on a loaded page; the FESTMIH and congress sites carry no count. I recorded the midpoint 1,400 rather than the top of the range, and flagged it: this is a range across two prior editions, not a count of one meeting.
ratio_rationale: Judged 45%, against ESCMID 40% and SOT 46%. ECTMIH is a biennial academic research congress of modest size whose programme is assembled almost entirely from submitted abstracts and delegate-organised sessions; it has no industry exhibition or CME market pulling in non-presenting attendees, and its audience is researchers and PhD students from tropical-medicine institutes, the cohort that submits at the highest rate. Small research-driven meetings of this shape sit well above the big clinical congresses.
programme_evidence: Described as a congress covering 'development, global research ethics and the role of social sciences in global health research' organised by FESTMIH member institutes — a research-society congress, not a taught course.
character_evidence: https://www.festmih.eu/pages/biennial-congress — ECTMIH runs an open call for abstracts and for organised sessions each biennium.

conference: Chinese Medical Doctor Association Annual Conference
attendance_method: No figure found. Rungs tried: A1 — no exhibitor prospectus exists for a CMDA-level annual conference; A2/A3 — cmda.net was loaded via curl (the meeting-notices index at /hyjhcx/) and returned no attendance text; A4 — no venue or convention-bureau source. Underlying problem, and it is a definitional one: the Chinese Medical Doctor Association (中国医师协会) does not hold one society-wide scientific annual conference with a published headcount. What it holds is dozens of separate 分会年会 (division annual conferences) — 呼吸 (respiratory, CACP), 眼科 (ophthalmology, COA), 介入 (interventional, CCI), 儿科 (paediatrics) and so on — each with its own attendance. Search snippets asserting figures such as 'over 8,000' for dermatology/orthopaedic/anaesthesia divisions and '12,000' for the neurology division traced to a 2017 university news article about the association's divisions, not to any CMDA annual-conference page, and I did not confirm them on a loaded page, so they are not recorded. Absence of evidence is not evidence the meeting is small — a CMDA division conference is plausibly several thousand strong, and the parent body's own gathering may well be large; we simply have no sourced number, and the row may need re-specifying to name a particular division conference before it can be measured.
programme_evidence: Not established. Chinese division annual conferences of this type typically mix invited lectures with a 征文 (call for papers) track, but I confirmed nothing for the parent-body conference.

attendance_method: Advisory Board daily-briefing piece loaded via curl: 'At the 2025 HLTH conference, which ran from Oct. 19 to Oct. 22 in Las Vegas, over 12,000 attendees heard presentations from more than 400 speakers.' HLTH's own site (hlth.com/events/usa/, loaded) markets HLTH USA 2026 as '12,250+ Attendees' with '4,400+ C-Suite' — a forward projection, so it sits in alt_figures below the retrospective figure per the A2-over-A1 rule. Chief Healthcare Executive's piece 403s to both the fetch tool and curl with a browser UA, so its number was not used. Note this headcount is a trade-show total: it includes vendor and investor staff, who are most of the room.
ratio_rationale: Judged at the 0.5% floor — this is exactly the case the lowered floor exists for, and even 0.5% overstates it. The judgement is not about who the attendees are; it is that essentially no contributed science happens at HLTH. There is no call for abstracts anywhere on the site, no submission deadline, no author guidelines, no proceedings: the programme is 400+ invited speakers on curated stages, and the 12,000 headline is a trade-show gate count that includes vendor and investor booth staff and exhibition visitors, who are precisely the category the brief says to discount. EuroPCR at 6% is at least a medical teaching course attached to a specialty with a peer-reviewed literature; HLTH is a commercial health-technology trade conference. The honest count of submitted abstracts is zero.
programme_evidence: 'over 12,000 attendees heard presentations from more than 400 speakers' — a speaker-led stage programme; hlth.com sells Investor Connect, Attendee Meetup and sponsor activations, not sessions.
character_evidence: https://hlth.com/events/usa/ — no call for abstracts, no submission deadline, no author guidelines anywhere on the site; the programme is built from invited speakers and sponsors.

attendance: over 4,000 participants from around the world
attendance_rung_name: institutional press coverage of that edition
attendance_method: Karolinska Institutet news page on AMEE 2025 (Barcelona, 23-27 Aug 2025) loaded via curl: 'The conference brought together over 4,000 participants from around the world and offered both future outlooks and important discussions on the role of education in a rapidly changing healthcare.' Basis UNSPECIFIED and worth flagging: AMEE 2025 ran a parallel online track (the AMEE FAQ page describes live streams and dedicated online short-communication sessions), so this figure may be virtual-inclusive. KI is a participating institution rather than the organiser, but it is a named, accountable source and the number is on the page I loaded. No figure was found on amee.org itself.
ratio_rationale: Judged 55%, above ATS 50% and AAIC 50%. AMEE's programme is almost entirely built from submitted work — short communications, research papers, posters, conference workshops and 'Patil' style sessions all come through the abstract call, and the plenary/keynote layer is thin by comparison (two keynotes framed the 2025 meeting). Medical-education researchers also submit at unusually high rates because presenting is how educators justify the travel; this is the same dynamic that puts GSA at 119%. Held to 55% rather than higher because AMEE's 4,000 includes a substantial cohort of faculty-development attendees who come to learn from the courses.
programme_evidence: The AMEE 2025 in-person provisional programme is organised around short communications, research papers, posters and conference workshops — contributed formats — with only two framing keynotes.
character_evidence: https://amee.org/amee-2025-archive/amee-2025-faqs/ — AMEE runs an open annual call for abstracts across multiple presentation formats, with author notification and a published programme.

attendance: more than 2,300 delegates from over 100 countries
attendance_rung_name: post-congress statement on the congress site
attendance_method: The WFOT Congress 2026 home page was loaded via curl and now carries a post-congress thank-you: 'thanks to everyone who contributed to the success of the 19th WFOT Congress in Bangkok, Thailand. This year's event brought together more than 2,300 delegates from over 100 countries, featured speakers representing more than 70 countries - and welcomed sponsors from across the globe.' Congress ran 9-12 February 2026. Worth recording: a search snippet asserted '2,400 delegates from 96 countries' for this same congress; the page itself says 2,300 and 100+ countries. I used the page.
ratio_rationale: Judged 50%, against ATS 50% and AAIC 50%. A quadrennial world congress in a small allied-health profession is the classic 'come because you got accepted' meeting: the congress site's navigation is built around Abstracts, Presenter Guidelines, Abstract Reviewers and Posters, the call for abstracts closed nearly a year ahead (14 March 2025) with author notification in July 2025, and for occupational therapists travelling to Bangkok an accepted presentation is usually what unlocks institutional funding. Not pushed to the GSA/ESPGHAN band because WFOT also draws a large clinician-practitioner audience attending purely for CPD.
programme_evidence: Congress site menu: Abstracts / Presenter Guidelines / Abstract Reviewers / Programme / Posters — a programme assembled from reviewed submissions.
character_evidence: https://wfotcongress2026.org/ — Key Dates table: 'March 14th 2025 Call for Abstracts closes; July 11th 2025 Author Notification; September 1st 2025 Programme released online'.

attendance: as many as 1600 annual attendees from more than 70 countries
attendance_method: mascc.org 403s to curl with a browser UA but the fetch tool retrieved it; the Annual Meeting page states the meeting has grown to draw 'as many as 1600 annual attendees from more than 70 countries'. This is a ceiling ('as many as') and a typical-year description rather than a count of one edition, and the same page lists the audience as including industry representatives and patient partners alongside clinicians and researchers, so it is not a clean delegate count. The 2025 meeting-highlights page (Seattle, 26-28 June 2025) also 403s to curl and carried no figure via the fetch tool.
ratio_rationale: Judged 45%, between ESCMID 40% and SOT 46%. MASCC/ISOO is a small multidisciplinary research society whose annual meeting is built on a large submitted-abstract poster programme relative to its size — supportive-care research is produced largely by nurses, pharmacists and allied health professionals, and this meeting is the one venue for that work, so they submit to it at a high rate. (My first pass held this down to 40% on the grounds that the 1,600 headline folds in allied-health attendees and patient partners; the allied-health half of that was wrong — they are the core submitting community here, not a dilution — so the row moves up. The only genuinely non-submitting slice is whatever exhibitor booth staff sit inside the figure, which the source does not quantify and which is small for a meeting this size.)
programme_evidence: Society page describes the meeting as bringing together clinicians, researchers and advocates around 'scientific sessions, interactive discussions, and networking events' — a research-society meeting rather than a taught course.
character_evidence: https://mascc.org/meetings/annual-meeting/ — MASCC runs an open annual abstract call; abstracts are published in Supportive Care in Cancer.

attendance_method: ESCRS's own 'REGISTRATION REPORT - 31 July 2025' PDF was downloaded via curl and read with pdftotext. Its first table, 'General Figures / Types of attendance / Number of attendance', reads: Delegates 7'260 | Industry 3'384 | Total 10'644. This is exactly the EUROSPINE trap the brief warns about, and the source hands us the clean split: converting the 10,644 headline instead of the 7,260 delegate count would overstate this row by 47%, because the 3,384 industry registrations are company staff who never submit. Caveat that lowers confidence: the report is dated 31 July 2025 for a congress held 12-16 September 2025, so it is a mid-registration snapshot and the final delegate count will be somewhat higher than 7,260 — the figure is a floor, not a final count.
ratio_rationale: Judged 21% of the 7,260 delegates, landing on ASTRO 21%, with honest uncertainty across roughly 18-26%. The discount applied here is only the legitimate one: the source's own 3,384 'Industry' registrations are company badges — booth and commercial staff who cannot submit — so the delegate figure is the right denominator and no further markdown follows. Against that base, the case for the lower end is that ESCRS shares EuroPCR's DNA, a surgical congress whose centre of gravity is instructional courses, wetlabs, video symposia and live surgery. The case for the higher end is that, unlike EuroPCR, ESCRS runs a substantial free-paper and poster programme on its own open call, and a congress of 7,260 cataract and refractive surgeons generates a lot of submitted clinical series. 21% is my central read; I have not shaded it in either direction.
programme_evidence: ESCRS programmes are built around instructional courses, wetlabs and video symposia alongside free-paper and poster sessions; the 3,384 industry registrations against 7,260 delegates show how commercially weighted the congress is.
character_evidence: https://congress.escrs.org/ — an open abstract call for free papers and posters runs alongside a large invited instructional-course programme.

attendance_rung_name: post-meeting statement on the society's meeting page
attendance_method: ors.org 2026 Annual Meeting page loaded via curl, post-meeting banner: 'Thank you for joining us at the ORS 2026 Annual Meeting, held March 27-31, 2026, in Charlotte, North Carolina. This meeting brought together more than 2,000 attendees and featured 332 podium talks, 2,010 posters, and 11 Spotlight Talks, delivering a dynamic scientific program.' The same sentence gives both the headcount and the presentation counts, so no second source was needed. 'More than 2,000' is a floor, and the basis is not stated.
ratio_rationale: Not a gut call — the source states both sides. 332 podium talks + 2,010 posters + 11 Spotlight Talks = 2,353 presentations against 'more than 2,000' attendees, i.e. 117%, right alongside GSA 119%. That is the correct shape for ORS: it is a basic-science research society, not a clinical college, its meeting exists so that labs can present, and prolific labs present several abstracts each from one or two travelling authors — which is exactly how a ratio exceeds 100%. Counts accepted presentations, so submissions were higher still.
programme_evidence: 2,353 contributed presentations against a handful of plenaries; the site navigation is Daily Podium Presentations / Posters / Late Breaking Posters / Author Index / Keyword Index.
character_evidence: https://www.ors.org/2026abstracts/ and https://www.ors.org/2027-call-for-abstracts/ — a standing annual open Call for Abstracts with a General Call and a Late-Breaking call, both shown as closed for 2026 on the meeting page.

attendance: 3,500+ Anticipated Total Attendance; 2,400+ Anticipated Professional Attendance; 150+ Anticipated Exhibiting Companies
attendance_year: prospectus figures, page carries 2024 framing and 2023 demographics
attendance_method: AABB exhibitor prospectus site (run by A.F. Fassano & Co, AABB's exhibit sales agent) loaded via curl. 'Attendee Statistics' block: '3,500+ Anticipated Total Attendance | 2,400+ Anticipated Professional Attendance | 150+ Anticipated Exhibiting Companies | 55,000 Net Sq. Ft. of Exhibits', with 'More than 73% of professional attendees are involved in the purchasing process. Based on 2023 registered attendee demographics.' This is the EUROSPINE trap again and the prospectus hands us the split itself: 2,400 professional attendees versus a 3,500 total, so roughly 1,100 of the headline are exhibitor and industry staff. I converted the professional figure. Two caveats that cap confidence: every number is 'Anticipated', i.e. a projection rather than a count, and the page mixes years (a 2026 prospectus title, 2024 body copy, 2023 demographics base), so the edition it describes is ambiguous.
ratio_rationale: Judged 15% of the 2,400 professional attendees, just above ASHP 12%, and I am torn between roughly 12% and 20%. AABB is the closest analogue we have to ASHP in the anchor list: a workforce meeting for a regulated practice community whose draw is standards updates, regulatory sessions, hands-on workshops and CME. The reason to hold it near ASHP is that little of the programme is contributed science — most sessions are invited and standards-driven. The reason not to go lower is that AABB does run a real annual abstract call with a poster floor, and against a professional base of only 2,400 a few hundred posters is a meaningful share. The exhibitor and industry staff who genuinely cannot submit are already excluded by using the 2,400 professional figure rather than the 3,500 total, so no further discount is applied. (My first pass reasoned partly from the '73% are involved in purchasing' statistic; that describes what attendees do for their employer, not whether they do research, so I have dropped it as a basis and the row moves up slightly.)
programme_evidence: Described as 'the leading educational conference for professionals in transfusion medicine and biotherapies, including scientific sessions, hands-on workshops, and regulatory updates'; 55,000 net sq ft of exhibits for a 2,400-strong professional audience is an unusually commercial ratio.
character_evidence: https://www.aabb.org/annual-meeting/ — AABB runs an annual abstract call feeding poster and oral abstract sessions alongside a predominantly taught educational programme.

attendance_method: No figure found. Rungs tried: A1 — no IPRAS exhibitor prospectus exists on the open web; A2/A3 — icoplast.org was loaded via curl and carries no attendance figure anywhere on the landing page; A4 — no venue or convention-bureau source surfaced. There is a structural reason this row is hard, and it should be flagged to the orchestrator rather than treated as a small-meeting finding: IPRAS (the International Confederation for Plastic, Reconstructive and Aesthetic Surgery, founded 1955, quadrennial World Congress) has effectively been superseded by ICOPLAST, the International Confederation of Plastic Surgery Societies, which now runs the confederation's world congress — the 3rd ICOPLAST World Congress was held in Cape Town in September 2025. A search snippet asserted 'almost 500 participants from more than 50 countries' for that congress; I could not confirm it on any page I loaded, so it is not recorded as a figure. Absence of evidence is not evidence the meeting is small — though the confederation model (a congress of national societies, with a Council of National Delegates) does point to a delegate-society meeting rather than a mass congress, and the row may need re-specifying as ICOPLAST before it can be measured.
programme_evidence: Not established. ICOPLAST's site organises education around Webinars, Symposiums, Congress and Visiting Professor programmes — an education-and-advocacy confederation rather than an abstract-driven research society, which if it holds would put any successor congress toward the curated end.

attendance: more than 1400 participants from 87 countries, and 400 speakers across 70 sessions
attendance_method: 'Scientific highlights of the 8th World One Health Congress, Cape Town, South Africa 2024', One Health Outlook (doi 10.1186/s42522-025-00143-x). The Springer page redirects to an auth endpoint and PubMed's HTML did not yield the abstract to curl, so I pulled the full record from the Europe PMC REST API, which returned the published abstract verbatim: 'It brought together more than 1400 participants from 87 countries, and 400 speakers across 70 sessions.' That is a retrospective, peer-reviewed account written by the congress's own scientific leadership — the most accountable rung available here. A search snippet also asserted '600 scientific posters'; I did not confirm that on a loaded page and have not recorded it as a figure.
ratio_rationale: Judged 50%, against ATS 50% and AAIC 50%. The arithmetic in the source alone gets most of the way there: 400 speakers across 70 sessions is already 29% of the 1,400 participants before a single poster is counted, and the congress runs an open call for abstracts feeding a substantial poster programme on top of that. A transdisciplinary research congress with no exhibition, no CME market and a self-funding academic audience travelling to Cape Town is the classic 'accepted abstract is what pays for the trip' meeting. Held at 50% rather than higher because One Health also draws policy, NGO and government-agency delegates who attend to negotiate rather than present.
programme_evidence: 400 speakers across 70 sessions plus an open abstract call and poster programme, against fourteen keynote lectures — the invited layer is thin relative to the contributed one.
character_evidence: http://globalohc.org/8WOHC — WOHC2024 ran an open call for abstracts and published an Abstract Book.

conference: IMSH (International Meeting on Simulation in Healthcare)
attendance: over 4,200+ attendees, 130+ Exhibiting Companies, 800+ total education events
attendance_method: HealthySimulation.com's opening-day report on IMSH 2026 (San Antonio, 10-14 Jan 2026) loaded via curl: 'The Society for Simulation in Healthcare (SSH) has over 5,340 members, with 300+ SSH Accredited Centers, 5,500+ SSH Certified Professionals. IMSH 2026: Unbound has over 4,200+ attendees, 130+ Exhibiting Companies, and offered 800+ total education events.' Basis unstated and very likely inclusive of the 130+ exhibiting companies' booth staff, so this is a padded headline I could not clean — SSH's own imsh2026.org About and Expo Hall pages were both loaded and carry no headcount, and the imsh2027.org Expo Hall page gives only exhibitor satisfaction statistics. A search snippet claiming IMSH 2025 exceeded 4,770 was not confirmed on a loaded page and is not recorded.
ratio_rationale: Judged 20%, against ASTRO 21% and ERA 21%, and with the padded headcount noted above pushing the true share slightly higher than 20% of the people actually in the room. IMSH does run an open Call for Content, but the crucial detail from SSH's own FAQ is what that call covers: 'courses, research abstracts, SimVentor innovations'. The overwhelming majority of the 800+ education events are hands-on workshops, immersive courses and demonstrations — submitted, peer-reviewed, but not abstracts — and the audience is simulation-centre educators and technicians who come for the training. Research abstracts are a real but minority track, which is exactly the ASTRO shape: a solid contributed science layer inside a large teaching programme.
programme_evidence: SSH FAQ: 'IMSH features a diverse, multi-day program including hands-on workshops, immersive courses, peer-reviewed presentations, research abstracts, SimVentor innovations, panel discussions, and interactive demonstrations'; the Expo Hall page sells 'three days of immersive experiences, including workshops, speakers, and education sessions'.
character_evidence: https://imsh2026.org/about — 'SSH opens a Call for Content each spring, inviting submissions for courses, research abstracts, SimVentor innovations' (shown Closed for IMSH 2026): an open call, but one dominated by course submissions rather than abstracts.

attendance: attended by almost 1,500 participants from all over the world
attendance_method: ESTES News 5/2015 PDF downloaded via curl and read with pdftotext. Congress report, opening line: "'Save lives, share knowledge' - This was the motto of the 16th European Congress of Trauma and Emergency Surgery organized in the capital of The Netherlands and attended by almost 1,500 participants from all over the world." A naming note the orchestrator needs: the European Trauma Society merged into ESTES (European Society for Trauma and Emergency Surgery), and this congress line now runs as ECTES — the 24th edition was Aachen 2025 and the 25th is Stockholm 2026, held jointly with the 8th World Trauma Congress. So this row's meeting still exists, under a different name. No recent headcount was found: estes-congress.org's welcome-note page and estesonline.org were both loaded and carry none. The figure is from 2015 and is therefore a decade old, which is why confidence is LOW; the joint 2026 World Trauma Congress edition will be materially larger than this.
ratio_rationale: Judged 40%, against ESCMID 40%. The 2015 congress report describes a heavily contributed programme — free papers, a poster exhibition large enough to run best-poster awards and 'bullet talk' sessions for selected posters, plus delegate-submitted 'Worst-Case Scenario' case presentations — set against 25 instructional course lecture sessions from the five ESTES sections and pre-courses such as Definitive Surgical Trauma Care. That is the ESCMID balance exactly: a mid-sized European specialty congress where most of the science is submitted, but a substantial taught course layer draws attendees who present nothing. Applied to 1,500 participants, not to a padded total, since no industry split was published.
programme_evidence: 2015 congress report: poster sessions with bullet talks and best-poster awards, delegate-presented case sessions, and free-paper sessions on trauma systems and registries, alongside 25 instructional course lecture sessions.
character_evidence: https://estes-congress.org/programme-abstracts/abstract-submission — open annual call for abstracts, accepted for Oral, Quickshot (mini-oral) or ePoster presentation, with the best 15-20 invited to submit full manuscripts to Trauma Surgery and Acute Care Open.
